      - article:
        - heading "Understand" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Volume is the integral of cross-sectional area across the interval.
      - article:
        - heading "▣ Formula & Rule" [level=3]
        - text: Volume by Slicing (Cross-Sectional Area Method)
        - paragraph: If a solid is sliced perpendicular to the x-axis and the cross-sectional area at x is A(x), then
        - strong:
          - text: V = ∫
          - subscript: a
          - superscript: b
          - text: A(x)dx
        - list:
          - listitem: Each slice has area A(x).
          - listitem: Thickness of each slice is dx.
          - listitem: Total volume is the integral from a to b.
      - article:
        - heading "◉ Worked Example" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find the volume of the sphere generated by revolving y=√(9−x²) about the x-axis.
        - text: "Cross-sectional area: A(x)=π(9−x²)"
        - paragraph:
          - text: V=∫
          - subscript: −3
          - superscript: "3"
          - text: π(9−x²)dx
        - paragraph:
          - text: =π[9x−x³/3]
          - subscript: −3
          - superscript: "3"
        - strong: V=36π cubic units
      - article:
        - heading "⚠ Common Misconception" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Using y instead of A(x) in the integral.
        - text: "Wrong: V=∫"
        - subscript: −3
        - superscript: "3"
        - text: y dx
        - paragraph: Why wrong? y is a length, not an area. Volume requires the area of each cross-section.
      - heading "▣ Try It Yourself" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Find the volume formed by revolving y=√(16−x²) about the x-axis.
